If we use relativistic k = E/(ħc) = 50 / 197.3 = 0.253 fm^{-1}, 1/k = 3.95 fm, we got 35.9.
If we use relativistic momentum: E_total = 50 MeV? If kinetic energy = 50 MeV, total = 50.511, p = sqrt(50.511^2 - 0.511^2) ≈ 50.508 MeV/c, k = 50.508/197.3 = 0.256, 1/k = 3.9.

What if we use the reduced mass? The target is a nucleus, so reduced mass μ ≈ m_e. Same.

What if the "scattering amplitude" is defined with an extra factor of 2? Some books define f(θ) = (1/k) Σ (2l+1) e^{iδ_l} sin δ_l P_l(cosθ). Then Im f(0) = (1/k) Σ (2l+1) sin^2 δ_l. That's what I used. But some other books define f(θ) = (1/(2ik)) Σ (2l+1) (e^{2iδ_l} - 1)
